original_question: For Wigner ensembles whose equilibrium measure is supported on more than one interval, can one prove universality in the bulk and at all spectral edges, and can one also analyze parameter regimes in which intervals in the support of the equilibrium measure open and close?
target_in_paper: Problem 2 (universality for random matrix theory (RMT)), specifically the open-problem paragraph on page 5 beginning: "Another open problem in RMT is to prove universality, in the bulk and at (all) the edges, for Wigner ensembles in the case that the equilibrium measure for the ensemble is supported on more than one interval..."
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the right target almost verbatim: the paper asks about Wigner ensembles whose equilibrium measure is supported on more than one interval, seeks universality in the bulk and at all edges of that support, and also asks for an analysis of parameter variation under which support intervals open and close (Problem 2, p. 5).
missing_details: The paper is asking about universality of microscopic local eigenvalue statistics, not just an unspecified global notion of universality (Problem 2, pp. 2-3, 5).
The asymptotic regime n→∞ is implicit throughout the universality discussion and should be made explicit in a stand-alone formulation (Problem 2, pp. 2-3).

The relevant Wigner ensembles are the general real symmetric or complex Hermitian ensembles whose matrix entries are independent subject only to the symmetry constraint; your draft does not spell this out (Problem 2, p. 2).
"All spectral edges" should be made precise as all endpoints of the support of the equilibrium measure (Problem 2, p. 5).
The paper asks not only to analyze but to "analyze and control" parameter-dependent changes in the support as the underlying matrix distributions vary (Problem 2, p. 5).

The nearby context clarifies the intended critical phenomena via the unitary invariant quartic example V(x)=-ax^2+bx^4 with b>0 fixed and a critical value a_c where the support changes from one interval to two; at a=a_c a different critical universality class appears. Your draft omits this orienting example (Problem 2, p. 5).

The paper does not add extra moment, smoothness, or normalization hypotheses in this particular open-problem formulation, so a faithful rewrite should preserve that informal level of generality rather than invent new assumptions (Problem 2, pp. 2, 5).
refined_question: For general Wigner ensembles—namely n×n real symmetric or complex Hermitian random matrices whose entries are independent subject only to the symmetry constraint—can one prove universality of the microscopic local eigenvalue statistics, both in the bulk and at every endpoint of the support of the ensemble’s equilibrium measure, in the case where that support consists of more than one interval, and can one also analyze and control parameter-dependent regimes in which, as the underlying matrix distribution varies, intervals in the support of the equilibrium measure open and close?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s actual intent. The nearest official formulation is not a conjecture or theorem but an informal open problem in Problem 2. The paper first frames Problem 2 as universality for local eigenvalue statistics of Wigner ensembles and describes Wigner ensembles as having independent entries subject to symmetry (Problem 2, pp. 2-3). It then isolates the multi-interval-support case as a separate open problem and immediately adds the parameter-varying opening/closing of support intervals (Problem 2, p. 5). The quartic unitary invariant example with V(x)=-ax^2+bx^4, b>0, and a critical value a_c supplies the precise nearby model for the support transition and the associated critical regime that motivates the Wigner question (Problem 2, p. 5). This paper does not contain items labeled Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3; the correct target is the relevant paragraph in Problem 2.
